title: The story of Adire: indigo, cassava and resistance
excerpt: How Yoruba women turned a simple dye technique into one of West Africa's most recognisable art forms.
author: Haanta Editorial
body: Adire means 'tie and dye' in Yoruba. For more than a century, women in Abeokuta and Ibadan have used cassava paste, raffia and stitching to resist indigo dye, creating patterns that carry names, proverbs and family histories.
Each design is made by hand, which means no two pieces are exactly alike. Small variations in colour and line are a mark of the maker, not a flaw.
Today a new generation of designers is cutting adire into tailored shirts, wrap dresses and two-piece sets, taking the craft from the market stalls of Itoku to wardrobes around the world.
Caring for adire is simple: wash cold, by hand, inside out, and dry away from direct sun so the indigo stays deep for years.

title: How to measure yourself for made-to-order pieces
excerpt: A five-minute guide to bust, waist, hips and length so your made-to-order piece fits like it was made for you. Because it was.
author: Haanta Fit Team
body: Use a soft tape measure and wear light clothing. Measure in inches, keep the tape level and snug but not tight.
Bust: around the fullest part of your chest. Waist: around your natural waist, the narrowest part of your torso. Hips: around the fullest part of your hips and seat.
Height and lengths: stand straight against a wall without shoes. For dress length, measure from the top of the shoulder to where you want the hem to fall.
Not sure? Add a note when you add the piece to your bag. Our designers read every note before they start cutting.

title: From Lagos to your door: how Haanta shipping works
excerpt: Why some pieces arrive in days and others in a few weeks, and how duties are already included in your price.
author: Haanta Customer Care
body: Some of our stock lives at the Haanta hub in Houston, Texas. Those pieces ship within the US in 2-5 working days.
Most pieces ship directly from our designers' studios in Nigeria. Standard delivery takes 10-21 days; DHL Express takes 2-3 days once the piece is ready.
Made-to-order and pre-order pieces need production time first. The product page always shows an estimate.
Prices include import duties and taxes for the US and Canada, so there is nothing extra to pay on delivery.
